course_description:
This course offers clinical experience in the assessment and management of either adult or paediatric clients. Students are given moderate-low levels of direction and support from on-site Practice Educators.

This course offers clinical experience in the assessment and management of either adult or paediatric clients. The focus of the clinical learning is on the integration of knowledge and skills in the description and analysis of communication disorders and the role of the student as a clinical practitioner. Students are given moderate-low levels of direction and support from on-site Practice Educators.

course_aims: This course complements the placement experience students gain in SPCH3113. Students join clinicians in their usual workplace, and will be expected to interview, assess, diagnose, treat clients, and report on assessment and intervention. Students are given moderate-low levels of direction and support from their on-site Practice Educators. Clinical skills and competencies will be assessed using Speech Pathology Australia’s Professional Standards for Speech Pathologists in Australia (2020) or the Competency Assessment in Speech Pathology (COMPASS®3.0) (Speech Pathology Australia, 2013).

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate culturally safe communication and interpersonal skills with clients, family members and other professionals and peers (SPA PS 1.1-1.7)
Apply clinical reasoning to select and administer appropriate assessments and analyse and interpret data to identify client communication and swallowing needs (SPA PS 3.2, 3.3)
Design and implement evidence-based, person- and family-centred management plans as required to support client communication and swallowing needs (SPA PS 1.1-1.7, 2.5, 3.4, 3.5)
Critically reflect on your professional abilities to set goals and professional development plans in the context of life-long learning (SPA PS 2.1, 2.2, 2.3)
Produce written and verbal clinical records which are appropriate to the clinical setting and the audience (SPA PS 1.2, 1.3, 1.5, 3.3)
Engage in interprofessional collaborative practice to achieve respectful partnerships across professions (SPA PS 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 2.5, 2.6)

assessment_details.task_description: You will attend tutorials to support your preparation for placement. To develop your reflective practice skills, you will complete reflection tasks in Weeks 2-6. Reflection Part 1 must be submitted via the SPCH3213 Blackboard site before each tutorial in Weeks 2-6. You will respond to prompts such as: What I think I know - identify two (2) things you know or have experienced on placement about this topic What I want to find out - identify two (2) things you would like to find out from the tutorial. Reflection Part 2 must be submitted by the end of the tutorial, following discussion of your reflections with a peer. You will respond to a prompt such as: What I know now - what you have learnt from the tutorial Across the 5 weeks of tutorials, you are required to submit a total of 3 reflections (both part A and B) . Each reflection is PASS/FAIL MUST PASS and must be passed to pass the course overall. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Placement Students will be placed in a sessional speech pathology (internal or external) clinic with a practice educator. Students will be placed in a sessional adult or paediatric placement with a practice educator. Placement duration will be either: • 1 full day per week for 8 weeks of the semester or; • half a day per week for 13 weeks of the semester (Weeks 1-13). Start/finish times for placements will vary depending on the placement allocated to each student.
Tutorials Students will attend tutorials (2-hours) in Weeks 1-8 to support preparation for placement. Tutorials will cover a range of professional practice topics.
